task.title: Set up reader sign-in with OIDC
task.shortdesc: Readers sign in through any OpenID Connect provider. matches them to the readers you registered by verified email.

step.cmd: Register a web application with your identity provider, with the redirect URI $PUBLIC_URL/auth/callback.
Set the provider details on the web service.

stepxmp.codeblock: OIDC_ISSUER=https://login.example.com OIDC_CLIENT_ID=... OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=... # OIDC_SCOPES=openid email profile (the default) # OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME=Acme SSO ("Sign in with Acme SSO" on the sign-in page)

step.cmd: Register each reader by email, in their organization.
Restart the web service and sign in at $PUBLIC_URL/auth/login.

info.p: The sign-in page lists every configured provider: Sign in with GitHub (see ), Sign in with your OIDC provider, and, with OPEND_DEV_LOGIN outside production, Demo readers. With exactly one provider and no demo readers it goes straight to that provider. The OIDC flow starts at /auth/oidc.

ul.li: The flow is the authorization code flow with PKCE, state and nonce.

A reader already linked to the provider's issuer and subject is signed in. Otherwise, a verified email that matches a registered reader links that reader to the subject on first sign-in. An unverified email never matches.
Anyone else sees "No access" and is not signed in.
The session is a signed, HttpOnly cookie holding only the reader id, valid for 12 hours. Entitlements are re-read through a short cache that is cleared as soon as an admin changes them.
A reader whose organization has no entitlements yet sees "No access yet".
Pages show the reader's name and Sign out in the header, and in the menu on narrow screens. Signing out is a form post carrying the session's CSRF token; opening /auth/logout only asks.

On a private site every page sends signed-out visitors to the sign-in page, which returns them to the page afterwards. On a public site they read the public view and can sign in from the header. The return address is always a path on the same site. See .
